How to read this research

What do Group 1 and Group 2 mean?

The groups describe the type of coordinating arrangement, not its quality, effectiveness or score. Both may have a documented role in shaping a road safety policy, strategy, programme or action plan.

01

Group 1

Government-established coordinating bodies

Official national or subnational councils, commissions, committees and formally designated government coordination or implementation groups. The body has a traceable governmental mandate or appointment to coordinate road safety work. The government may still be the separate authority that formally adopts the strategy.

Examples: Serbia's government coordinating body; Poland's National Road Safety Council; France's Interministerial Road Safety Committee. Tasmania is a subnational case in this group.

24of 27 mechanisms
02

Group 2

Other policy-contributing coordination arrangements

Documented intergovernmental, cross-agency, advisory or parliamentary arrangements that contribute to road safety policy outputs but do not fit the conventional statutory executive road safety council model used for Group 1. Their remit may be narrower than nationwide implementation.

Examples: Canada's Council of Motor Transport Administrators, Sweden's Vision Zero cooperation forum (GNS), and Uganda's parliamentary road safety forum.

3of 27 mechanisms

Classification boundary: Group 1 does not imply direct control over every implementing ministry; Group 2 does not mean an organization is unofficial or ineffective. Membership, policy authority, action ownership and actual delivery are evaluated separately.

How the dashboard pages connect

How is this different from “Bodies & Strategies”?

The Bodies & Strategies directory is the wider evidence register. It asks which coordinating body is linked to which named policy output, and what the documented relationship is. This Country Case Studies page takes the 26 linked countries into a deeper, mechanism-based assessment against the ideal governance framework.

195 countriesBodies & Strategies directory

Catalogue institutions and published outputs. Distinguish verified formulation, approval or stewardship from an unverified association.

›
26 linked countriesEvidence-based selection

Use documented links between a coordinating arrangement and a substantive strategy, policy, target or action plan. A document alone is not proof of council authorship.

›
27 mechanismsCountry Case Studies

Examine membership (17 domains), planned intervention responsibilities (72 of 85 cells), source evidence and gaps. The two US state mechanisms are assessed individually.

Two different questions: Bodies & Strategies establishes attribution; Case Studies examines institutional and intervention alignment. Neither page, by itself, proves that planned measures were implemented or caused better safety outcomes. Use the Bodies & Strategies tab to inspect the original country-to-document relationships.

Interpretation: A counts only a documented exact planned responsibility. P records partial documentary alignment. Neither proves implementation, financing, effectiveness or reductions in road fatalities. N/A is an evidence gap, not an observed failure. The framework has 85 possible cells per mechanism, of which 13 have no specified intervention and are excluded from the 72-cell comparison. No global inference from seven reviewed mechanisms is warranted.

How are these statistics calculated?

Each study record represents one coordinating mechanism, not always one whole country: the United States contains separate New York and Washington mechanisms. Group and maturity counts are based on 27 profiles. The global directory status counts use 195 country entries. The evidence-match bar uses only the seven detailed reviewed profiles and their 72 defined interventions each (504 records). Older aggregate scores are not included in this bar. An N/A indicates insufficient source-level verification, not evidence of zero activity. Thirteen framework positions are undefined, and therefore never counted as eligible interventions.

How to interpret the country evidence

Institutional representation: Formal member means the domain has a documented statutory or officially appointed place in the coordinating body. Functional partner means a relevant organization has a documented technical, advisory or delivery relationship, without a confirmed formal seat. Not verified means available sources do not establish that link.

Intervention responsibilities: Exact planned match means the documented planned responsibility closely meets the specified ideal action. Partial documented match means only part of the requirement is supported. Not verified means sufficient evidence has not been found. Not re-audited means an earlier assessment exists but the individual record has not been reconciled.

These labels describe documentary alignment, not proof of implementation or impact. Select a country to open it inline; select it again or use Close country details to return to the full list.

Methodology: source-instrument attribution is separate from delivery and outcomes; 13 undefined framework cells are excluded from the 72-intervention denominator. No endorsement or official UN affiliation is implied.
